wirecraft.config.title: WireCraft
wirecraft.config.enabled.tooltip: When on, the mod can route the Minecraft connection through a VPN tunnel. Turn off to fully bypass the mod.
wirecraft.config.connectOnStartup.toolti: Starts the tunnel as soon as the game launches, if the primary WireGuard profile has a private key, peer public key, and endpoint set.
wirecraft.config.autoDownloadWireproxy.t: Downloads the wireproxy helper binary from its GitHub releases on first use. Leave off to point at a binary you downloaded and verified yourself.
wirecraft.config.showPublicIp.tooltip: Looks up the IP the game's connection currently exits as. Uses the same tunnel as the game (via the SOCKS5 proxy) when WireGuard is connected, so it reflects what the Minecraft server actually sees.
wirecraft.config.wireguard.importPath: Import: path to a WireGuard .conf (then click Done)
wirecraft.config.wireguard.reset.tooltip: Clears every field and generates a brand new keypair. Turn this on, then click Done to apply.
wirecraft.config.wireguard.yourPublicKey: Your public key (share this with the server admin)
wirecraft.config.wireguard.resetToastMes: Profile reset with a fresh keypair
wirecraft.config.bindings.hint: Auto-connect this profile whenever you join a specific server.
wirecraft.config.status.hint: Toggle the tunnel any time from the VPN button on the multiplayer server list screen.
wirecraft.consent.message: WireCraft can tunnel the game's connection through WireGuard. To do that without needing admin rights, it uses a small helper program called wireproxy. The mod can download it automatically from its official GitHub releases, or you can provide your own copy instead.
wirecraft.download.title: Downloading wireproxy
